description: How the posts of the last 7, 30 or 90 days did, the same numbers as the Results page: how many went out, their likes, comments and shares, views and reach where a network reports them, the same for the period before, each network’s share, the five posts that did best with their links, the times of the week the posts did best at (bestTimes, from the last 90 days; times is empty until enough posts have results), what a post got on average with each hashtag (hashtags), tracked short-link clicks (shortLinks), connected-account follower counts and period growth (audience), and account sync status (sync). Pass source ("all", "spica" or "native", default "all") to include synced posts published directly on connected accounts alongside Spica posts, or filter to either. When sync.accountsSynced < sync.accountsEligible, call results_sync once to pull full account history and follower snapshots (after which accounts refresh daily). Use it when the user asks how their posts or accounts are doing or what to post more of. notReported names networks posted to that gave no numbers. A Spica post is read 1 hour, 1 day, 3 days and 7 days after it goes out, and synced accounts refresh all recent posts daily. Where a Google Business Profile is connected, google holds what the profile itself got, by Google’s own count, over the same number of days ending three days ago (period): how many people called (calls), asked for directions (directions) or opened the website from it (websiteClicks), and how often it was seen (views, split into viewsInSearch and viewsInMaps). totals adds up every profile that was read and profiles lists each one; a profile whose state is no_reading gave no numbers just now, so say that and ask again later, and reconnect means the user reconnects it on their account page. google is null when no profile is connected. Where Google Search Console is connected, searchConsole holds the website’s Google Search performance over the same period ending three days ago: totals and previous ({clicks, impressions, ctr, position}), top search terms (queries) and top landing pages (pages), plus state (read, no_reading or reconnect). Part of Studio and Pro. Changes nothing.

brandId.description: The brand this is for, by its id from brands_list. Needed when the login has more than one brand; with one brand it can be left out.

days.description: How far back to look: 7, 30 or 90 days. 30 when left out.

source.description: Which posts to include: "all" (Spica + synced native posts, default), "spica", or "native".
